Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 109, verses 1–6:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Kafirun

It is Meccan, and its verses are six.

Ibn Kathir said: It is established in Sahih Muslim, from Jabir, that "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this surah and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) in the two rak'ahs of the tawaf."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited both of them in the two rak'ahs of Fajr."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Umar that "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited in the two rak'ahs before Fajr and the two rak'ahs after Maghrib, some twenty or about ten times, 'Say: O you disbelievers' and 'Say: He is Allah, the One.'"

Imam Ahmad also narrated from al-Harith ibn Jibillah, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, teach me something to say when I go to sleep. He said: When you take your bed at night, recite 'Say: O you disbelievers,' for it is a disavowal of shirk."

It has already been mentioned in a hadith that "it is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." In al-Lubab it is said: The reason for this is that the Qur'an comprises command and prohibition, and each of these is divided into what relates to the deeds of the hearts and what relates to the deeds of the limbs. Thus four categories arise. This surah comprises the prohibition of worshipping other than Allah Most High, which belongs to belief, and that is an act of the hearts. Thus this surah is a quarter of the Qur'an according to this division. Another secret will come in the tafsir of al-Ikhlas.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[1–6] "Say: O you disbelievers. I do not worship what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."

"Say: O you disbelievers" means: the polytheists who deny the truth whose proof has become clear and whose path has become evident.

"I do not worship what you worship" means: of the gods and idols, now.

"Nor are you worshippers of what I worship" means: now.

"Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped" means: in what I will do in the future, "what you have worshipped" means: in the past.

"Nor are you worshippers of what I worship" means: in what you will do forever, "what I worship" means: in what I will do in the future, "what you have worshipped" means: now and in what I will do in the future. This is how Imam Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it. Then he said: This was said in this manner because the address from Allah was to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning specific individuals among the polytheists, whom He knew would never believe, and this had already been decided in His prior knowledge. So He commanded His Prophet ﷺ to despair them of what they hoped for and what they whispered to themselves. That thing would neither come from Him nor from them at any time. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ despaired of their faith despite his hope in it, and of their ever prospering. So they remained as they were, not prospering and not succeeding, until some of them were killed by the sword on the day of Badr, and some perished in disbelief before that. Then he narrated from Ibn Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Mina, who said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and Umayyah ibn Khalaf met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad! Come, let us worship what you worship and you worship what we worship, and let us share with you in all our affairs. If what you have brought is better than what is in our hands, we will have shared it with you and taken our portion of it; and if what is in our hands is better than what is in your hands, you will have shared with us in our affairs and taken your portion of it." So Allah revealed "Say: O you disbelievers," the surah. And in another narration: Allah revealed this surah concerning that. And His saying: "Say: Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?" [az-Zumar: 64] "Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful." [az-Zumar: 66]. End.

It is also said: the last two sentences negate worship in the present, just as the first two negate it in the future. Abu al-Su'ud said: He did not say "what I have worshipped" in order to match "what you have worshipped," because they were known before the mission for worshipping idols, whereas he, peace be upon him, was not at that time known for worshipping Allah Most High. The use of "ma" in "what I worship" rather than "man" is because the intended meaning is description, as if it were said: "what I worship of the Great Object of worship, whose greatness cannot be measured." It is also said that "ma" is verbal-masdariyyah, meaning: I do not worship your worship, and you do not worship my worship. It is also said: the first two are in the sense of "alladhi," and the latter two are masdariyyah. 

It is also said: His saying, Exalted is He, "Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped," is an emphasis of His saying, "I do not worship what you worship," and His saying, "Nor are you worshippers of what I worship," is a second emphasis of a similar statement mentioned first. End.

Ibn Kathir related from Imam Ibn Taymiyyah that the intended meaning of "I do not worship what you worship" is the negation of the act, since it is a verbal sentence; and "Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped" is the negation of his acceptance of that altogether, since negation by a nominal sentence is stronger. So it negates both the act and his being capable of it, and its meaning is negation of occurrence and also negation of legal possibility. This is a good view.

The Imam preferred that "ma" in the first two be relative and in what follows be masdariyyah. He said: The implication of the first two sentences is complete difference in the object of worship, and the implication of the latter two is complete difference in the worship itself. Thus our object of worship is not one, nor is our worship one; for my object of worship is that One God, exalted above any peer or intercessor, transcending manifestation in any specific form, extending His bounty to everyone who sincerely devotes himself to Him, and seizing by the forelock everyone who rejects the truthful messengers who convey from Him; whereas what you worship is contrary to that. My worship is sincerely for Allah alone, while your worship is mixed with shirk and accompanied by heedlessness of Allah Most High; so it is not truly called worship. Where is it from my worship? His saying, Exalted is He, "For you is your religion," confirms His saying, "I do not worship what you worship," and "Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped," just as His saying, "And for me is my religion," confirms His saying, "Nor are you worshippers of what I worship." The meaning is that your religion, which is shirk, is confined to being yours, and does not extend to being mine too, as you hope; for that is impossible. And my religion, which is tawhid, is confined to being mine, and does not extend to being yours; so there is no sharing between it and what you are upon.

Admonition:

Ibn Kathir said: Imam al-Shafi'i and others took as evidence this noble verse, "For you is your religion, and for me is my religion," that all disbelief is one religion, so Jews inherit from Christians and vice versa, when there is between them a lineage or a cause by which inheritance is made; for all religions other than Islam are like one thing in falsehood. Ahmad ibn Hanbal and those who agreed with him held that Christians do not inherit from Jews, nor the reverse, based on the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of two different religions do not inherit from one another."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 109, verses 1–6:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Kafirun

It is Meccan, and its verses are six.

Ibn Kathir said: It is established in Sahih Muslim, from Jabir, that "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this surah and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) in the two rak'ahs of the tawaf."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited both of them in the two rak'ahs of Fajr."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Umar that "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited in the two rak'ahs before Fajr and the two rak'ahs after Maghrib, some twenty or about ten times, 'Say: O you disbelievers' and 'Say: He is Allah, the One.'"

Imam Ahmad also narrated from al-Harith ibn Jibillah, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, teach me something to say when I go to sleep. He said: When you take your bed at night, recite 'Say: O you disbelievers,' for it is a disavowal of shirk."

It has already been mentioned in a hadith that "it is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." In al-Lubab it is said: The reason for this is that the Qur'an comprises command and prohibition, and each of these is divided into what relates to the deeds of the hearts and what relates to the deeds of the limbs. Thus four categories arise. This surah comprises the prohibition of worshipping other than Allah Most High, which belongs to belief, and that is an act of the hearts. Thus this surah is a quarter of the Qur'an according to this division. Another secret will come in the tafsir of al-Ikhlas.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[1–6] "Say: O you disbelievers. I do not worship what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."

"Say: O you disbelievers" means: the polytheists who deny the truth whose proof has become clear and whose path has become evident.

"I do not worship what you worship" means: of the gods and idols, now.

"Nor are you worshippers of what I worship" means: now.

"Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped" means: in what I will do in the future, "what you have worshipped" means: in the past.

"Nor are you worshippers of what I worship" means: in what you will do forever, "what I worship" means: in what I will do in the future, "what you have worshipped" means: now and in what I will do in the future. This is how Imam Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it. So they remained as they were, not prospering and not succeeding, until some of them were killed by the sword on the day of Badr, and some perished in disbelief before that. Then he narrated from Ibn Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Mina, who said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and Umayyah ibn Khalaf met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad!
